# Goal: Cross-Harness Capability Parity (CHP)

**Purpose.** Make Claude Code CLI, Claude Desktop, Codex CLI, and the Codex app carry — as far as each architecturally *can* — the same **skills, tools, and functionality** Luke has built in `my-pi` + `pi-mono-fork`, then **measure** parity with one command, **confirm** it with evidence, and **maintain** it with an automated drift gate + propagation pipeline.

**How to use this doc.**
- §A is the copy-paste **goal prompt**.
- §B–§I are the spec: the parity model, success definition, acceptance, measurement, architecture, phases, non-negotiables, risks.
- §J is the **baseline scorecard** captured 2026-06-22 (real numbers — re-run the scanner to refresh).
- Appendix = grounded tool/path reference so the executing agent doesn't hallucinate the tooling.

**Status:** spec authored; Phase 0 (scanner v0) shipped — `scripts/harness-parity-scan.mjs`. Phases 1–4 not started.

---

## §0 — The reframing that makes this tractable

"Parity" is **not one thing**. Luke's Pi surface splits into three portability tiers, and the honest goal differs per tier. Forcing tier-3 into tier-1 is how this turns into an infinite project.

| Tier | What it is | Parity means | Target harnesses |
|---|---|---|---|
| **T1 — Portable** | Skills (markdown `SKILL.md` + `references/`) | The *same skill files* present & loadable | CC, Codex, Pi (all support a skills dir). **Desktop cannot** — no skills dir. |
| **T2 — Adaptable** | Pi tools that are really CLI/HTTP under a thin Pi wrapper: `fuse`, `advisor`, `semantic_grep`, `task-tools`, tokenjuice, OTel | An **equivalent MCP server or CLI** exposed to the harness | CC, Codex, Desktop (MCP is the universal seam) |
| **T3 — Pi-native** | Runtime behavior fused to Pi/claude-bridge: cache-base-prompt boundary, memory-v3 injection, fork-mode sibling cache, deferred-tool coordination, `setActiveTools` guard, goal state machine, worktree mutation blocker | A **documented native equivalent** (e.g. Codex has native memories/goals; CC has hooks) **or an accepted N/A** — never a port | per-harness; mostly N/A |

The whole project hangs on this: **drive T1 to ~100% mechanically, expose the worthwhile T2 tools via MCP once and wire everywhere, and for T3 maintain a documented equivalence map — don't chase ports that can't exist.** The hard architectural fact: **Claude Desktop's only extensibility surface is MCP servers** — so Desktop parity is bounded to T2 + whatever skills we choose to serve *through* an MCP "skills" server.

---

## §A — The Goal Prompt (paste this)

> Build the **Cross-Harness Capability Parity (CHP)** system described in `my-pi/docs/goals/goal-cross-harness-parity.md`. Work phase by phase (§F); each phase ships a deliverable **and** its verification before the next starts. Do not claim a phase done without the evidence named in its "Verify" line.
>
> The system must let me, with one command: (1) **measure** parity — a read-only scanner emits a scorecard of skills/MCP/hooks/commands/agents coverage per harness (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, Pi) against the canonical source of truth, classifying each capability into the §0 tiers; (2) **confirm** parity — a CI gate (`check:harness-parity`) fails when a harness drifts below its declared tier target, with the drift rendered to a committed report; (3) **close gaps** — drive T1 (skills) to ~100% via an idempotent propagation pipeline with per-agent targeting, expose chosen T2 tools as a single MCP server wired into every harness, and record T3 capabilities in an equivalence map (native-equivalent / accepted-N/A); (4) **maintain** it — the gate runs in `gate:ci` and a `weekly-review` cadence catches drift as skills/tools are added.
>
> Honor the §G non-negotiables (measure before claiming, read-only scanner with no model/API calls, three-tier honesty — no T3 ports, MCP-once-wire-everywhere for T2, single source of truth for skills, every recurring action is a script wrapper). Reuse existing tooling — extend `scripts/pi-setup-lib.mjs` (the static catalog scanner) and its `registry.generated.json` schema, the `drift.generated.md` output surface, `scripts/skills` (symlink propagation), the `prototypes/skill-sync` engine, and `gate:ci`. Only the new code is the harness-aware scan layer, the MCP exposure of T2 tools, and the propagation `--agent` targeting. When all phases are green, write the runbook (§F Phase 5) and report the final scorecard.

---

## §B — Definition of success

Success = Luke can run a **repeatable, evidence-backed loop** that:

1. **Measures** parity per harness in one command, tier-classified, against the canonical SoT.
2. **Confirms** parity in CI — a gate fails on drift below each harness's declared tier target, drift rendered to a committed report.
3. **Closes** the gaps: T1 skills at the agreed coverage on every skills-capable harness; the chosen T2 tools reachable as MCP in CC, Codex, and Desktop; T3 capabilities each marked native-equivalent or accepted-N/A in a committed map.
4. **Maintains** itself: adding a skill or tool to the SoT and re-running propagation + scan brings every harness back to target with **no manual symlinking**, and the gate catches anyone who forgets.

"Done" is not "configs touched." Done is: the §C checklist is green with the §D evidence committed, and the §H drill passes.

---

## §C — Acceptance checklist (every item needs evidence)

| # | Requirement | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| C1 | Parity scanner exists, read-only | `scripts/harness-parity-scan.mjs --json` runs from a clean worktree, makes no model/API calls, mutates nothing; emits the §D scorecard schema |
| C2 | Tier classification | Every measured capability tagged T1/T2/T3; the T3 equivalence map (`docs/pi-setup/harness-equivalence.md`) lists each Pi-native capability × harness as native-equiv / accepted-N/A |
| C3 | Scanner covers 4 harnesses | Scorecard has rows for Pi, Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex with skills/MCP/hooks/commands/agents surfaces; Desktop correctly shows skills=N/A, MCP-only |
| C4 | Drift gate | `npm run check:harness-parity` exits non-zero when any harness is below its declared target; passes when at/above; drift rendered to `docs/pi-setup/generated/harness-parity.generated.md` |
| C5 | T1 skill parity closed | Skills-capable harnesses (CC, Codex, Pi) at the agreed coverage of the canonical SoT (target ≥99%, justified exclusions listed); zero dangling symlinks |
| C6 | Propagation pipeline | One idempotent command syncs the SoT to a chosen `--agent` (claude-code/codex/pi/all); re-running is a no-op; a `status`/`diff` subcommand reports per-harness missing/extra/dangling |
| C7 | T2 tools exposed | ≥1 chosen adaptable Pi tool (e.g. `fuse` or `advisor`) packaged as an MCP server and wired into CC (`mcpServers`), Codex (`[mcp_servers]`), and Desktop (`claude_desktop_config.json`); the scanner counts it present in all three |
| C8 | New-capability drill | Adding one skill to the SoT and one tool to the MCP server, then re-running propagation + scan, brings all harnesses to target with **zero manual edits** (demonstrated in §H) |
| C9 | Maintenance wiring | `check:harness-parity` is in `gate:ci`; the cadence is documented in `weekly-review`; the runbook covers measure / close-gap / add-skill / add-tool / read-scorecard |
| C10 | Auditability | The scorecard is committed per run under `docs/pi-setup/generated/`; `git log` reconstructs parity over time |

---

## §D — How parity is measured (no vibes)

**The scorecard contract** (`harness-parity-scan.mjs --json`, `schemaVersion: 1`): per harness, per surface (`skills`, `mcp`, `hooks`, `commands`, `agents`, `features`):
- `supported: bool` — does the harness *architecturally* carry this surface? (Desktop skills → `false`.)
- For skills: `{total, canonicalCovered, canonicalTotal, parityPct, missing[], extra[], dangling[]}` vs the canonical SoT.
- For MCP/hooks/commands/agents: configured names + counts.

**Parity targets** (declared per harness, gate-enforced in C4):
- **T1 skills** — CC / Codex / Pi: `parityPct ≥ 99` of the canonical set minus a committed exclusion list (worktree-local, harness-specific, or package-declared skills). `dangling == 0` always.
- **T2 MCP** — the chosen CHP MCP server present in CC, Codex, Desktop.
- **T3** — presence in the equivalence map, not a numeric threshold.

**Drift gate** (`check:harness-parity`, exit≠0 ⇒ red): any skills-capable harness below its T1 target, any dangling symlink, or the CHP MCP server missing from a T2 target. Rendered to `harness-parity.generated.md`.

**Honest exclusions, never silent.** A skill legitimately absent from a harness (e.g. a Pi-only orchestration skill on Codex) goes in the committed exclusion list with a one-line reason. "Missing and unexplained" fails the gate; "missing and listed" passes. No silent truncation of coverage.

---

## §E — Architecture (grounded in existing tools)

Four components. **Reuse first** — the only new code is the harness-aware scan layer, the T2 MCP server, and propagation `--agent` targeting.

**A. Parity scanner** — *new glue, extends the catalog model.* `scripts/harness-parity-scan.mjs` (shipped, v0). Reads canonical SoT + each harness's skills dir and config (`~/.claude/settings.json`, `~/.codex/config.toml` + `hooks.json`, `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json`, `~/.pi/agent/settings.json`). Emits the §D scorecard. Next: fold its observations into `scripts/pi-setup-lib.mjs`'s `registry.generated.json` (add a `buildHarnessSnapshot()` beside `buildSnapshot()`) so parity lives in the same CMDB as the Pi catalog, and render `harness-parity.generated.md` (today a placeholder lives at `docs/pi-setup/generated/drift.generated.md`).

**B. T1 propagation** — *extend `scripts/skills` + `prototypes/skill-sync`.* Today `scripts/skills link --apply` symlinks the whole SoT into all three harness roots; it has no `--agent` filter and no `status`/`diff`. Add: per-agent targeting (`--agent claude-code|codex|pi|all`), a `status`/`diff` subcommand (the read side the scanner already computes), and dangling-link repair. The tested `prototypes/skill-sync/sync.mjs` diff-cache engine is the basis for the eventual `npx skills` CLI that syncs **remote** runtimes (Mac Mini, pods) — local stays symlinks.

**C. T2 MCP exposure** — *new, small.* Package the worthwhile adaptable tools (start with one: `fuse` or `advisor`) as a single **CHP MCP server** (stdio). Wire it into all three MCP-capable harnesses' configs. One server, wired everywhere = the cheapest path to tool parity *and* the only path that reaches Desktop. Pi keeps using its native extension; the MCP server wraps the same underlying CLI/logic so behavior matches.

**D. T3 equivalence map** — *docs, not code.* `docs/pi-setup/harness-equivalence.md`: a table of each Pi-native capability × harness → `native-equivalent: <what>` / `accepted-N/A: <why>`. This is the parity *contract* for the un-portable tier; the scanner links to it so "not measured here" is explicit, not a gap.

**E. Maintenance** — *extend `gate:ci` + `weekly-review`.* Add `check:harness-parity` to the `gate:ci` chain; document the weekly cadence in the `weekly-review` skill. Adding a skill/tool to the SoT → propagation + scan → gate stays green.

```
  canonical SoT (~/Projects/personal/skills) ──┐
                                                ▼
   (B) propagation ──► CC / Codex / Pi skills dirs ──┐
   (C) CHP MCP server ─► CC / Codex / Desktop mcp ──► (A) scanner ──► scorecard + drift report
   (D) T3 equivalence map ────────────────────────────┘                    │
                                                                            ▼
                                                            (E) check:harness-parity in gate:ci + weekly-review
```

---

## §F — Phased plan (deliverable + verification each)

- **Phase 0 — Scanner v0.** *(SHIPPED.)* Read-only `harness-parity-scan.mjs` over 4 harnesses; baseline scorecard (§J). **Verify:** runs clean, no mutations, real numbers — done.
- **Phase 1 — Tiering + targets + gate.** Write the §0 tier tags into the scanner output; declare per-harness targets + the exclusion list; render `harness-parity.generated.md`; add `check:harness-parity` (exit≠0 on drift). **Verify:** gate red on a planted missing skill, green after propagation (C1–C4).
- **Phase 2 — T1 closed.** Extend `scripts/skills` (`--agent`, `status`/`diff`, dangling repair); reconcile drift to target; commit the exclusion list. **Verify:** all skills-capable harnesses ≥99%, 0 dangling, re-run is a no-op (C5, C6).
- **Phase 3 — T2 one tool everywhere.** Package `fuse` (or `advisor`) as the CHP MCP server; wire into CC + Codex + Desktop; scanner counts it in all three. **Verify:** scorecard shows the server present in all three MCP-capable harnesses; the tool actually invokes in each (C7).
- **Phase 4 — T3 map + new-capability drill.** Author `harness-equivalence.md`; run the §H drill. **Verify:** §H green — add-skill + add-tool propagate with zero manual edits (C8).
- **Phase 5 — Maintenance.** Wire `check:harness-parity` into `gate:ci`; document `weekly-review` cadence; write the runbook. **Verify:** `gate:ci` includes the check; runbook covers all recurring actions (C9, C10).

---

## §G — Non-negotiables

1. **Measure before claiming** — no parity assertion without a committed scorecard.
2. **Scanner is read-only** — no model calls, no API calls, no mutation; safe from CI or any worktree.
3. **Three-tier honesty** — never attempt a T3 port; T2 goes through MCP once and is wired everywhere; T1 is the only tier driven to ~100%.
4. **Single source of truth for skills** — `~/Projects/personal/skills` is canonical; harnesses get propagated copies, never hand-edited.
5. **Exclusions are explicit** — a skill absent from a harness is either above-threshold-irrelevant (listed with a reason) or a gate failure. No silent coverage gaps.
6. **CLI wrappers for every recurring action** — scan, propagate, gate, add-skill, add-tool; no tribal incantations.
7. **Reuse over reinvention** — extend `pi-setup-lib`/`scripts/skills`/`skill-sync`/`gate:ci`/`drift.generated.md`; new code limited to the harness scan layer, the T2 MCP server, and `--agent` targeting.
8. **Desktop is MCP-bounded** — accept it; don't fake a skills dir it doesn't have.

---

## §H — Final verification drill (proves the goal)

1. `node scripts/harness-parity-scan.mjs` → baseline scorecard, committed.
2. `npm run check:harness-parity` → green at target; plant a missing skill → red; propagate → green again.
3. Add one new skill to the SoT; run propagation `--agent all`; re-scan → all skills-capable harnesses back to target, **zero manual edits**.
4. Add one tool to the CHP MCP server; restart harnesses; re-scan → server still counted present in CC + Codex + Desktop.
5. `git log docs/pi-setup/generated/` reconstructs the parity history.
6. Open `harness-equivalence.md` → every T3 Pi-native capability has a native-equiv or accepted-N/A entry per harness.

Goal achieved ⇔ all six green and §C fully evidenced.

---

## §I — Risks & mitigations

- **Scope creep into "port everything"** → the §0 tiering is the firewall; T3 is documented, never ported.
- **Desktop expectations** → state up front Desktop = MCP-only; skills reach it (if at all) via an MCP skills server, not a dir.
- **Drift gate too brittle** → targets are `≥pct` with an explicit exclusion list, not exact-set equality; new SoT skills don't break the gate until propagated, but the report flags them.
- **Codex model-family split** → Codex is OpenAI-only; skills/tools assuming Claude behavior are T3-flagged (native-equiv via `claude-code` MCP shim or accepted-N/A), not forced.
- **Remote runtimes** (Mac Mini, pods) out of local symlink reach → deferred to the `npx skills`/`skill-sync` remote path; local parity first.
- **MCP server auth/secrets** → the CHP server reads from `~/.profile`/`op` like other tools; never bake secrets into configs.

---

## §J — Baseline scorecard (captured 2026-06-22)

```
  canonical skills SoT: ~/Projects/personal/skills (108 skills)

  harness             skills                mcp  hooks  cmds  agents
  ------------------------------------------------------------------
  Pi (pi-mono-fork)   105/108 (97.2%) +22   N/A  N/A    N/A   N/A
  Claude Code CLI     104/108 (96.3%)       0    9      8     1
  Codex CLI/app       102/108 (94.4%) +2    13   4      N/A   2
  Claude Desktop      N/A (no dir)          0    N/A    N/A   N/A
```

Reading it:
- **T1 (skills) is already close** — 94–97% on all three skills-capable harnesses. Drift is modest: the recurring "missing" set (`eval`, `sevh`, `progressive-disclosure-workspace`, `herdr`, `docs`, `maintainer-orchestrator`) is mostly new/worktree-local or harness-specific — exactly the exclusion-list vs propagate decision Phase 2 settles. Pi's `+22 extra` are package-declared skills (legitimate, not drift).
- **T2 (MCP tools) is the real asymmetry** — Codex carries **13** MCP servers; Claude Code's *global* config carries **0** (its session tools are project/harness-injected); Desktop **0**. This is the biggest, most actionable gap, and the one a single CHP MCP server fixes across all three.
- **Desktop is the structural floor** — skills N/A, MCP-only. Its parity ceiling is T2.
- **CC vs Codex hooks** — CC 9, Codex 4; both rich. Hooks are a T3-ish surface (lifecycle wiring), tracked in the equivalence map, not driven to numeric parity.

Re-run: `node scripts/harness-parity-scan.mjs` (table) or `--json` (machine).

---

## Appendix — Tool reference (real paths / commands)

**Parity scanner** — `my-pi/scripts/harness-parity-scan.mjs`. `node scripts/harness-parity-scan.mjs [--json]`. Read-only. Canonical SoT hardcoded to `~/Projects/personal/skills`.

**Catalog scanner (extend for CMDB integration)** — `my-pi/scripts/pi-setup-snapshot` → `scripts/pi-setup-lib.mjs` (`buildSnapshot()`). Emits `docs/pi-setup/generated/registry.generated.json` (`schemaVersion:1`, `safety:{modelCalls:false,apiCalls:false,livePiBoot:false}`). Catalog YAML at `docs/pi-setup/catalog/*.yaml` (capabilities/packages/extensions/tools/runtime-features/providers/bridges). Drift placeholder: `docs/pi-setup/generated/drift.generated.md`.

**Skill propagation (extend)** — `~/Projects/agent-scripts/scripts/skills` (Python, ~513 LOC). Subcommands today: `inventory`, `validate`, `add`, `inbox`, `link`. `link --apply` symlinks SoT → `~/.claude/skills`, `~/.codex/skills`, `~/.pi/agent/skills`. **No `--agent`, no `status`/`diff` yet** — Phase 2 adds them. The `npx skills` CLI referenced in CLAUDE.md **does not exist yet** — it's a forward spec for the remote path.

**Skill-sync engine** — `my-pi/prototypes/skill-sync/sync.mjs` (tested offline; version-diff/SHA-changeset/burst/prune). Basis for the future `npx skills` remote sync. Spec: `my-pi/docs/specs/skill-federation.md`, `docs/skill-store-federation-plan.md`.

**Harness configs (read by the scanner)** — CC: `~/.claude/settings.json` (`mcpServers`, `hooks`, `env`), `~/.claude/commands/`, `~/.claude/agents/`. Codex: `~/.codex/config.toml` (`[mcp_servers.*]`, `[features]`, `[[skills.config]]`), `~/.codex/hooks.json` (`{hooks:{...}}`), `~/.codex/skills/`, `~/.codex/agents/`. Desktop: `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` (`mcpServers` only). Pi: `~/.pi/agent/settings.json`, `~/.pi/agent/skills/`.

**Adaptable T2 tool candidates** — `fuse` (`~/.pi/agent/bin/fuse`, impl `my-pi/extensions/fusion/`), `advisor` (`my-pi/extensions/advisor/`), `semantic_grep` (`my-pi/extensions/pi-semantic-grep/`), `task-tools` (`my-pi/extensions/task-tools/`). Each is a thin Pi wrapper over portable logic → MCP-able.

**Pi-native T3 (equivalence-map only, do not port)** — cache-base-prompt boundary (`my-pi/extensions/cache-base-prompt/`), memory-v3 (`my-pi/extensions/pi-memory/`), dream-memory (`my-pi/extensions/dream-memory/`), fork-mode sibling cache + `setActiveTools` guard (`pi-mono-fork/packages/coding-agent/src/core/`), deferred-tool coordination (`my-pi/extensions/tool-search/`), goal state machine (`my-pi/extensions/pi-goal/`), worktree mutation blocker (`my-pi/extensions/pi-worktree/`). claude-bridge proxy (`pi-claude-bridge/`) is shared infra usable by *any* Anthropic-SDK client (CC included) — bridge-adjacent, not strictly Pi-native.

**Relation to SEVH** — the sibling goal `goal-agnostic-skill-eval-harness.md` measures skill **quality** across models. CHP measures cross-harness **coverage**. Complementary: SEVH says a skill is *good*; CHP says it's *present everywhere it should be*. Share the skills SoT and the `skill-workshop`/git provenance spine.

| C6 | Propagation pipeline | One idempotent command syncs the SoT to a chosen `--agent` (claude-code/codex/pi/all); re-running is a no-op; a `status`/`diff` subcommand reports per-harness missing/extra/dangling |
| C7 | T2 tools exposed | ≥1 chosen adaptable Pi tool (e.g. `fuse` or `advisor`) packaged as an MCP server and wired into CC (`mcpServers`), Codex (`[mcp_servers]`), and Desktop (`claude_desktop_config.json`); the scanner counts it present in all three |
| C8 | New-capability drill | Adding one skill to the SoT and one tool to the MCP server, then re-running propagation + scan, brings all harnesses to target with **zero manual edits** (demonstrated in §H) |
| C9 | Maintenance wiring | `check:harness-parity` is in `gate:ci`; the cadence is documented in `weekly-review`; the runbook covers measure / close-gap / add-skill / add-tool / read-scorecard |
| C10 | Auditability | The scorecard is committed per run under `docs/pi-setup/generated/`; `git log` reconstructs parity over time |

---

## §D — How parity is measured (no vibes)

**The scorecard contract** (`harness-parity-scan.mjs --json`, `schemaVersion: 1`): per harness, per surface (`skills`, `mcp`, `hooks`, `commands`, `agents`, `features`):
- `supported: bool` — does the harness *architecturally* carry this surface? (Desktop skills → `false`.)
- For skills: `{total, canonicalCovered, canonicalTotal, parityPct, missing[], extra[], dangling[]}` vs the canonical SoT.
- For MCP/hooks/commands/agents: configured names + counts.

**Parity targets** (declared per harness, gate-enforced in C4):
- **T1 skills** — CC / Codex / Pi: `parityPct ≥ 99` of the canonical set minus a committed exclusion list (worktree-local, harness-specific, or package-declared skills). `dangling == 0` always.
- **T2 MCP** — the chosen CHP MCP server present in CC, Codex, Desktop.
- **T3** — presence in the equivalence map, not a numeric threshold.

**Drift gate** (`check:harness-parity`, exit≠0 ⇒ red): any skills-capable harness below its T1 target, any dangling symlink, or the CHP MCP server missing from a T2 target. Rendered to `harness-parity.generated.md`.

**Honest exclusions, never silent.** A skill legitimately absent from a harness (e.g. a Pi-only orchestration skill on Codex) goes in the committed exclusion list with a one-line reason. "Missing and unexplained" fails the gate; "missing and listed" passes. No silent truncation of coverage.

---

## §E — Architecture (grounded in existing tools)

Four components. **Reuse first** — the only new code is the harness-aware scan layer, the T2 MCP server, and propagation `--agent` targeting.

**A. Parity scanner** — *new glue, extends the catalog model.* `scripts/harness-parity-scan.mjs` (shipped, v0). Reads canonical SoT + each harness's skills dir and config (`~/.claude/settings.json`, `~/.codex/config.toml` + `hooks.json`, `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json`, `~/.pi/agent/settings.json`). Emits the §D scorecard. Next: fold its observations into `scripts/pi-setup-lib.mjs`'s `registry.generated.json` (add a `buildHarnessSnapshot()` beside `buildSnapshot()`) so parity lives in the same CMDB as the Pi catalog, and render `harness-parity.generated.md` (today a placeholder lives at `docs/pi-setup/generated/drift.generated.md`).

**B. T1 propagation** — *extend `scripts/skills` + `prototypes/skill-sync`.* Today `scripts/skills link --apply` symlinks the whole SoT into all three harness roots; it has no `--agent` filter and no `status`/`diff`. Add: per-agent targeting (`--agent claude-code|codex|pi|all`), a `status`/`diff` subcommand (the read side the scanner already computes), and dangling-link repair. The tested `prototypes/skill-sync/sync.mjs` diff-cache engine is the basis for the eventual `npx skills` CLI that syncs **remote** runtimes (Mac Mini, pods) — local stays symlinks.

**C. T2 MCP exposure** — *new, small.* Package the worthwhile adaptable tools (start with one: `fuse` or `advisor`) as a single **CHP MCP server** (stdio). Wire it into all three MCP-capable harnesses' configs. One server, wired everywhere = the cheapest path to tool parity *and* the only path that reaches Desktop. Pi keeps using its native extension; the MCP server wraps the same underlying CLI/logic so behavior matches.

**D. T3 equivalence map** — *docs, not code.* `docs/pi-setup/harness-equivalence.md`: a table of each Pi-native capability × harness → `native-equivalent: <what>` / `accepted-N/A: <why>`. This is the parity *contract* for the un-portable tier; the scanner links to it so "not measured here" is explicit, not a gap.

**E. Maintenance** — *extend `gate:ci` + `weekly-review`.* Add `check:harness-parity` to the `gate:ci` chain; document the weekly cadence in the `weekly-review` skill. Adding a skill/tool to the SoT → propagation + scan → gate stays green.

```
  canonical SoT (~/Projects/personal/skills) ──┐
                                                ▼
   (B) propagation ──► CC / Codex / Pi skills dirs ──┐
   (C) CHP MCP server ─► CC / Codex / Desktop mcp ──► (A) scanner ──► scorecard + drift report
   (D) T3 equivalence map ────────────────────────────┘                    │
                                                                            ▼
                                                            (E) check:harness-parity in gate:ci + weekly-review
```

---

## §F — Phased plan (deliverable + verification each)

- **Phase 0 — Scanner v0.** *(SHIPPED.)* Read-only `harness-parity-scan.mjs` over 4 harnesses; baseline scorecard (§J). **Verify:** runs clean, no mutations, real numbers — done.
- **Phase 1 — Tiering + targets + gate.** Write the §0 tier tags into the scanner output; declare per-harness targets + the exclusion list; render `harness-parity.generated.md`; add `check:harness-parity` (exit≠0 on drift). **Verify:** gate red on a planted missing skill, green after propagation (C1–C4).
- **Phase 2 — T1 closed.** Extend `scripts/skills` (`--agent`, `status`/`diff`, dangling repair); reconcile drift to target; commit the exclusion list. **Verify:** all skills-capable harnesses ≥99%, 0 dangling, re-run is a no-op (C5, C6).
- **Phase 3 — T2 one tool everywhere.** Package `fuse` (or `advisor`) as the CHP MCP server; wire into CC + Codex + Desktop; scanner counts it in all three. **Verify:** scorecard shows the server present in all three MCP-capable harnesses; the tool actually invokes in each (C7).
- **Phase 4 — T3 map + new-capability drill.** Author `harness-equivalence.md`; run the §H drill. **Verify:** §H green — add-skill + add-tool propagate with zero manual edits (C8).
- **Phase 5 — Maintenance.** Wire `check:harness-parity` into `gate:ci`; document `weekly-review` cadence; write the runbook. **Verify:** `gate:ci` includes the check; runbook covers all recurring actions (C9, C10).

---

## §G — Non-negotiables

1. **Measure before claiming** — no parity assertion without a committed scorecard.
2. **Scanner is read-only** — no model calls, no API calls, no mutation; safe from CI or any worktree.
3. **Three-tier honesty** — never attempt a T3 port; T2 goes through MCP once and is wired everywhere; T1 is the only tier driven to ~100%.
4. **Single source of truth for skills** — `~/Projects/personal/skills` is canonical; harnesses get propagated copies, never hand-edited.
5. **Exclusions are explicit** — a skill absent from a harness is either above-threshold-irrelevant (listed with a reason) or a gate failure. No silent coverage gaps.
6. **CLI wrappers for every recurring action** — scan, propagate, gate, add-skill, add-tool; no tribal incantations.
7. **Reuse over reinvention** — extend `pi-setup-lib`/`scripts/skills`/`skill-sync`/`gate:ci`/`drift.generated.md`; new code limited to the harness scan layer, the T2 MCP server, and `--agent` targeting.
8. **Desktop is MCP-bounded** — accept it; don't fake a skills dir it doesn't have.

---

## §H — Final verification drill (proves the goal)

1. `node scripts/harness-parity-scan.mjs` → baseline scorecard, committed.
2. `npm run check:harness-parity` → green at target; plant a missing skill → red; propagate → green again.
3. Add one new skill to the SoT; run propagation `--agent all`; re-scan → all skills-capable harnesses back to target, **zero manual edits**.
4. Add one tool to the CHP MCP server; restart harnesses; re-scan → server still counted present in CC + Codex + Desktop.
5. `git log docs/pi-setup/generated/` reconstructs the parity history.
6. Open `harness-equivalence.md` → every T3 Pi-native capability has a native-equiv or accepted-N/A entry per harness.

Goal achieved ⇔ all six green and §C fully evidenced.

---

## §I — Risks & mitigations

- **Scope creep into "port everything"** → the §0 tiering is the firewall; T3 is documented, never ported.
- **Desktop expectations** → state up front Desktop = MCP-only; skills reach it (if at all) via an MCP skills server, not a dir.
- **Drift gate too brittle** → targets are `≥pct` with an explicit exclusion list, not exact-set equality; new SoT skills don't break the gate until propagated, but the report flags them.
- **Codex model-family split** → Codex is OpenAI-only; skills/tools assuming Claude behavior are T3-flagged (native-equiv via `claude-code` MCP shim or accepted-N/A), not forced.
- **Remote runtimes** (Mac Mini, pods) out of local symlink reach → deferred to the `npx skills`/`skill-sync` remote path; local parity first.
- **MCP server auth/secrets** → the CHP server reads from `~/.profile`/`op` like other tools; never bake secrets into configs.

Both the human table and machine JSON work, runnable via `npm run parity:scan`. Here's where the goal lands.

## Answer: how to get parity, measure it, and maintain it

The honest reframing that makes this tractable — **"parity" is three tiers, not one**, and forcing tier 3 to behave like tier 1 is how this becomes an infinite project:

| Tier | What | Parity means | Reaches |
|---|---|---|---|
| **T1 Portable** | Skills (`SKILL.md` markdown) | *Same files present* | CC, Codex, Pi — **not Desktop** (no skills dir) |
| **T2 Adaptable** | Pi tools that are CLI/HTTP under a thin wrapper (`fuse`, `advisor`, `semantic_grep`, `task-tools`) | *Equivalent MCP server* exposed | CC, Codex, **Desktop** (MCP is the universal seam) |
| **T3 Pi-native** | cache-base-prompt, memory-v3 injection, fork-mode sibling cache, deferred-tool coordination, goal state machine | *Documented native-equivalent or accepted N/A* — **never a port** | mostly N/A |

The decisive constraint: **Claude Desktop's only extensibility surface is MCP servers** — no skills dir, no hooks, no commands. Its parity ceiling is T2. Accept it; don't fake a skills dir.

## What I built (the "measure & confirm" foundation, working now)

[scripts/harness-parity-scan.mjs](scripts/harness-parity-scan.mjs) — read-only, no model/API calls, mutates nothing. `npm run parity:scan` (or `--json`). **Real baseline today:**

```
harness             skills                mcp  hooks  cmds  agents
Pi (pi-mono-fork)   105/108 (97.2%) +22   N/A  N/A    N/A   N/A
Claude Code CLI     104/108 (96.3%)       0    9      8     1
Codex CLI/app       102/108 (94.4%) +2    13   4      N/A   2
Claude Desktop      N/A (no dir)          0    N/A    N/A   N/A
```

What it reveals, contradicting the "skills are wildly drifted" assumption:
- **T1 skills are already ~94–97% everywhere** — modest drift, mostly new/worktree-local skills (`sevh`, `eval`, `progressive-disclosure-workspace`). Pi's `+22` are legit package-declared skills, not drift.
- **The real gap is T2/MCP tools** — Codex carries **13** MCP servers, Claude Code's *global* config carries **0** (its tools are project-injected), Desktop **0**. One CHP MCP server wired into all three fixes the most actionable gap *and* is the only thing that reaches Desktop.
- `npx skills` **doesn't exist yet** — CLAUDE.md references it as real, but the actual mechanism is `scripts/skills link` (manual symlink, no `--agent` targeting, no `status`/`diff`).

## The full spec (answers all three legs)

[goal-cross-harness-parity.md](docs/goals/goal-cross-harness-parity.md) — mirrors your SEVH spec's structure: tier model, acceptance checklist with evidence, the measurement contract, a phased plan, non-negotiables, the verification drill, and the committed baseline. Architecture **reuses existing scaffolding** (extends `pi-setup-lib.mjs`'s CMDB, the `drift.generated.md` surface, `scripts/skills`, the tested `prototypes/skill-sync` engine, `gate:ci`) — new code is limited to the scan layer (shipped), one T2 MCP server, and `--agent` propagation targeting.

- **Get parity** → Phase 2 drives T1 to ~100% via idempotent propagation; Phase 3 exposes one T2 tool as MCP everywhere; Phase 4 writes the T3 equivalence map.
- **Measure & confirm** → the scanner (done) + Phase 1 gate `check:harness-parity` (red on drift below per-harness target, with an explicit exclusion list).
- **Maintain** → Phase 5 wires the gate into `gate:ci` + a `weekly-review` cadence.

## Recommended next step

Phase 0 is shipped and proves the design. The next slice — **Phase 1: tier-tag the scanner output, declare per-harness targets + the exclusion list, render the drift report, add `check:harness-parity`** — is self-contained, in-repo, and completes the "confirm" leg. Phases 2–3 (mutating `agent-scripts` propagation + wiring MCP into three live configs) are more invasive and I'd want your go-ahead before touching live harness configs.

Say **go** and I'll build Phase 1 now. Nothing is committed — changes (scanner, spec, one `package.json` line) sit on the worktree branch.

**State: complete — Phase 0 (scanner + spec) shipped and verified; awaiting go/no-go on Phase 1.**

input.content:
# Harness equivalence map (T3 — Pi-native functionality)

Parity contract for the **non-portable** tier. These are Pi runtime behaviors fused to `pi-mono-fork` / `claude-bridge`. They are **not ported** — for each, parity means a *documented native equivalent* in the target harness, or an *accepted N/A* with a reason. The parity scanner (`scripts/harness-parity-scan.mjs`) does **not** gate these numerically; this doc is the source of truth.

See `docs/goals/goal-cross-harness-parity.md` §0 for the tier model. T1 (skills) and T2 (MCP tools) are gated by the scanner; T3 lives here.

Legend: ✅ native-equivalent (harness has its own mechanism) · 🟡 partial (covered via a hook/shim) · ⬜ accepted-N/A (no equivalent; not pursued).

| Pi-native capability | Pi impl | Claude Code | Codex | Claude Desktop |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Prompt-cache stability** (cache-base-prompt boundary, byte-stable prefix) | `extensions/cache-base-prompt`, fork `cache-affinity.ts` | ⬜ CC manages its own Anthropic caching; the boundary-relocation trick is Pi-only. claude-bridge breakpoints still apply if CC routes through it. | ⬜ OpenAI cache model differs; no instrumentation seam | ⬜ N/A |
| **Memory (cross-session)** | `extensions/pi-memory` v3 (SQLite injection) | 🟡 dream-memory `claude-code-hook.sh` injects `<persistent-memory>` at session start; plus CC's own memory files | ✅ native `memories` feature (`~/.codex/memories/`, rollout summaries) | ⬜ N/A (no hook/dir surface) |
| **Deferred tool loading** (`tool_search`) | `extensions/tool-search` + fork `deferred-tools.ts` | ✅ native deferred tools (`ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=true` in settings; `ToolSearch`) | ✅ native deferral (tool stubs) | ⬜ N/A |
| **Goal state machine** (`pi-goal`, `/goal`) | `extensions/pi-goal` | 🟡 goal via session Stop-hook (in use this session); no first-class goal tools | ✅ native `goals` feature | ⬜ N/A |
| **Multi-agent orchestration** (`Workflow`, `forkAgent`) | `extensions/pi-workflow` + fork executor | ✅ native subagents + `Workflow`/`Agent` tools + agent-teams (`CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1`) | ✅ native `multi_agent`/`multi_agent_v2` + `.toml` agent profiles (max_depth 1) | ⬜ N/A |
| **Context compaction** (tokenjuice / microcompact) | `extensions/tokenjuice`, `extensions/microcompact` | ✅ tokenjuice via `PreToolUse` Bash hook | ✅ tokenjuice via `PostToolUse` (`codex-post-tool-use`) | ⬜ N/A (no hook surface) |
| **Observability** (Opik / OTel spans) | `extensions/observability` | ✅ opik hooks (`opik-prompt/stop/session-end.sh`) | ✅ opik hooks + `notify` slot | ⬜ N/A |
| **Worktree mutation guard** (`pi-worktree`) | `extensions/pi-worktree` | ✅ native worktree support + can add a `PreToolUse` guard hook | ⬜ no worktree primitive | ⬜ N/A |
| **Fork-mode sibling cache** (placeholder parity, `setActiveTools` guard) | fork `agents/executor.ts`, `agent-session.ts` | ⬜ runtime-internal; no equivalent | ⬜ N/A | ⬜ N/A |
| **Background-bash wake-on-completion** | fork `tools/bash.ts` | ✅ CC wakes on background task completion natively | 🟡 depends on Codex runtime | ⬜ N/A |
| **Session recap / handoff nag** | `extensions/pi-recap`, `session-handoff-nag` | 🟡 via a `Stop`/`SessionEnd` hook if desired | 🟡 via `Stop` hook | ⬜ N/A |
| **Routines / scheduled runs** (`pi-routine`, `/loop`) | `extensions/pi-routine` | 🟡 `CronCreate`/`schedule` tools + launchd | 🟡 launchd timer | ✅ native Cowork scheduled-tasks UI |
| **claude-bridge proxy** (cache breakpoints, OTel, 1h TTL) | `pi-claude-bridge` | ✅ shared infra — any Anthropic-SDK client can route through it (`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`) | ⬜ OpenAI client, not Anthropic-SDK | 🟡 could route if pointed at the bridge |

## How to read this for parity decisions

- **✅ rows are done** — the harness already has the capability natively; no action.
- **🟡 rows are opportunities** — a hook or shim closes the gap if Luke wants it (these are the candidates for future hook-parity work, separate from the skill/MCP gate).
- **⬜ rows are settled** — accepted as not-applicable; do not attempt a port. Revisit only if the harness gains a new surface.

Claude Desktop is ⬜ for nearly everything by construction: its only extensibility surface is MCP servers, so the **only** way a T3 capability reaches Desktop is if it can be reframed as a T2 MCP tool (see the CHP MCP server, Phase 3).

_Maintained by hand; the scanner links here but does not generate it. Update when a harness gains/loses a native capability._

This redirected me from planning to actually executing the parity work.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **Three-tier parity model** (the central reframing): T1 Portable (skills/markdown — driven to full coverage), T2 Adaptable (Pi tools exposed as MCP servers — the universal seam, only thing reaching Claude Desktop), T3 Pi-native (runtime behavior fused to Pi/claude-bridge — documented equivalent or accepted N/A, NEVER ported).

   - **MCP** (Model Context Protocol) — the universal tool seam across all harnesses.

     - The core deliverable: read-only cross-harness parity scanner + gate. No model/API calls, no mutations. CI-safe.

# Harness equivalence map (T3 — Pi-native functionality)

Parity contract for the **non-portable** tier. These are Pi runtime behaviors fused to `pi-mono-fork` / `claude-bridge`. They are **not ported** — for each, parity means a *documented native equivalent* in the target harness, or an *accepted N/A* with a reason. The parity scanner (`scripts/harness-parity-scan.mjs`) does **not** gate these numerically; this doc is the source of truth.

See `docs/goals/goal-cross-harness-parity.md` §0 for the tier model. T1 (skills) and T2 (MCP tools) are gated by the scanner; T3 lives here.

Legend: ✅ native-equivalent (harness has its own mechanism) · 🟡 partial (covered via a hook/shim) · ⬜ accepted-N/A (no equivalent; not pursued).

| Pi-native capability | Pi impl | Claude Code | Codex | Claude Desktop |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Prompt-cache stability** (cache-base-prompt boundary, byte-stable prefix) | `extensions/cache-base-prompt`, fork `cache-affinity.ts` | ⬜ CC manages its own Anthropic caching; the boundary-relocation trick is Pi-only. claude-bridge breakpoints still apply if CC routes through it. | ⬜ OpenAI cache model differs; no instrumentation seam | ⬜ N/A |
| **Memory (cross-session)** | `extensions/pi-memory` v3 (SQLite injection) | 🟡 dream-memory `claude-code-hook.sh` injects `<persistent-memory>` at session start; plus CC's own memory files | ✅ native `memories` feature (`~/.codex/memories/`, rollout summaries) | ⬜ N/A (no hook/dir surface) |
| **Deferred tool loading** (`tool_search`) | `extensions/tool-search` + fork `deferred-tools.ts` | ✅ native deferred tools (`ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=true` in settings; `ToolSearch`) | ✅ native deferral (tool stubs) | ⬜ N/A |
| **Goal state machine** (`pi-goal`, `/goal`) | `extensions/pi-goal` | 🟡 goal via session Stop-hook (in use this session); no first-class goal tools | ✅ native `goals` feature | ⬜ N/A |
| **Multi-agent orchestration** (`Workflow`, `forkAgent`) | `extensions/pi-workflow` + fork executor | ✅ native subagents + `Workflow`/`Agent` tools + agent-teams (`CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1`) | ✅ native `multi_agent`/`multi_agent_v2` + `.toml` agent profiles (max_depth 1) | ⬜ N/A |
| **Context compaction** (tokenjuice / microcompact) | `extensions/tokenjuice`, `extensions/microcompact` | ✅ tokenjuice via `PreToolUse` Bash hook | ✅ tokenjuice via `PostToolUse` (`codex-post-tool-use`) | ⬜ N/A (no hook surface) |
| **Observability** (Opik / OTel spans) | `extensions/observability` | ✅ opik hooks (`opik-prompt/stop/session-end.sh`) | ✅ opik hooks + `notify` slot | ⬜ N/A |
| **Worktree mutation guard** (`pi-worktree`) | `extensions/pi-worktree` | ✅ native worktree support + can add a `PreToolUse` guard hook | ⬜ no worktree primitive | ⬜ N/A |
| **Fork-mode sibling cache** (placeholder parity, `setActiveTools` guard) | fork `agents/executor.ts`, `agent-session.ts` | ⬜ runtime-internal; no equivalent | ⬜ N/A | ⬜ N/A |
| **Background-bash wake-on-completion** | fork `tools/bash.ts` | ✅ CC wakes on background task completion natively | 🟡 depends on Codex runtime | ⬜ N/A |
| **Session recap / handoff nag** | `extensions/pi-recap`, `session-handoff-nag` | 🟡 via a `Stop`/`SessionEnd` hook if desired | 🟡 via `Stop` hook | ⬜ N/A |
| **Routines / scheduled runs** (`pi-routine`, `/loop`) | `extensions/pi-routine` | 🟡 `CronCreate`/`schedule` tools + launchd | 🟡 launchd timer | ✅ native Cowork scheduled-tasks UI |
| **claude-bridge proxy** (cache breakpoints, OTel, 1h TTL) | `pi-claude-bridge` | ✅ shared infra — any Anthropic-SDK client can route through it (`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`) | ⬜ OpenAI client, not Anthropic-SDK | 🟡 could route if pointed at the bridge |

## How to read this for parity decisions

- **✅ rows are done** — the harness already has the capability natively; no action.
- **🟡 rows are opportunities** — a hook or shim closes the gap if Luke wants it (these are the candidates for future hook-parity work, separate from the skill/MCP gate).
- **⬜ rows are settled** — accepted as not-applicable; do not attempt a port. Revisit only if the harness gains a new surface.

Claude Desktop is ⬜ for nearly everything by construction: its only extensibility surface is MCP servers, so the **only** way a T3 capability reaches Desktop is if it can be reframed as a T2 MCP tool (see the CHP MCP server, Phase 3).

_Maintained by hand; the scanner links here but does not generate it. Update when a harness gains/loses a native capability._

## codedb
codedb is a code-intelligence and context tool — not your editor. Use it to understand the codebase before you change it: search, symbol/caller lookup, dependency graph, outlines, and codedb_context for task-shaped orientation. Make edits with your own native file tools. codedb_edit is only a fallback for clients with no native editing.

## computer-use
You have a computer-use MCP available (tools named `mcp__computer-use__*`). It lets you take screenshots of the user's desktop and control it with mouse clicks, keyboard input, and scrolling.

**Pick the right tool for the app.** Each tier trades speed/precision against coverage:

1. **Dedicated MCP for the app** — if the task is in an app that has its own MCP (Slack, Gmail, Calendar, Linear, etc.) and that MCP is connected, use it. API-backed tools are fast and precise.
2. **Chrome MCP** (`mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`) — if the target is a web app and there's no dedicated MCP for it, use the browser tools. DOM-aware, much faster than clicking pixels. If the Chrome extension isn't connected, ask the user to install it rather than falling through to computer use.
3. **Computer use** — for native desktop apps (Maps, Notes, Finder, Photos, System Settings, any third-party native app) and cross-app workflows. Computer use IS the right tool here — don't decline a native-app task just because there's no dedicated MCP for it.

This is about what's available, not error handling — if a dedicated MCP tool errors, debug or report it rather than silently retrying via a slower tier.

**Look before you assert.** If the user asks about app state (what's open, what's connected, what an app can do), take a screenshot and check before answering. Don't answer from memory — the user's setup or app version may differ from what you expect. If you're about to say an app doesn't support an action, that claim should be grounded in what you just saw on screen, not general knowledge. Similarly, `list_granted_applications` or a fresh `screenshot` is cheaper than a wrong assertion about what's running.

**Loading via ToolSearch — load in bulk, not one-by-one:** if computer-use tools are in the deferred list, load them ALL in a single ToolSearch call: `{ query: "computer-use", max_results: 30 }`. The keyword search matches the server-name substring in every tool name, so one query returns the entire toolkit. Don't use `select:` for individual tools — that's one round-trip per tool.

**Access flow:** before any computer-use action you must call `request_access` with the list of applications you need. The user approves each application explicitly, and you may need to call it again mid-task if you discover you need another application.

**Tiered apps:** some apps are granted at a restricted tier based on their category — the tier is displayed in the approval dialog and returned in the `request_access` response:
- **Browsers** (Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Arc, etc.) → tier **"read"**: visible in screenshots, but clicks and typing are blocked. You can read what's already on screen. For navigation, clicking, or form-filling, use the claude-in-chrome MCP (tools named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`; load via ToolSearch if deferred).
- **Terminals and IDEs** (Terminal, iTerm, VS Code, JetBrains, etc.) → tier **"click"**: visible and left-clickable, but typing, key presses, right-click, modifier-clicks, and drag-drop are blocked. You can click a Run button or scroll test output, but cannot type into the editor or integrated terminal, cannot right-click (the context menu has Paste), and cannot drag text onto them. For shell commands, use the Bash tool.
- **Everything else** → tier **"full"**: no restrictions.

The tier is enforced by the frontmost-app check: if a tier-"read" app is in front, `left_click` returns an error; if a tier-"click" app is in front, `type` and `right_click` return errors. The error tells you what tier the app has and what to do instead. `open_application` works at any tier — bringing an app forward is a read-level operation.

**Link safety — treat links in emails and messages as suspicious by default.**
- **Never click web links with computer-use tools.** If you encounter a link in a native app (Mail, Messages, a PDF, etc.), do NOT `left_click` it. Open the URL via the claude-in-chrome MCP instead.
- **See the full URL before following any link.** Visible link text can be misleading — hover or inspect to get the real destination.
- **Links from emails, messages, or unknown-sender documents are suspicious by default.** If the destination URL is at all unfamiliar or looks off, ask the user for confirmation before proceeding.
- **Inside the Chrome extension** you can click links with the extension's tools, but the suspicion check still applies — verify unfamiliar URLs with the user.

**Financial actions - do not execute trades or move money.** Budgeting and accounting apps (Quicken, YNAB, QuickBooks, etc.) are granted at full tier so you can categorize transactions, generate reports, and help the user organize their finances. But never execute a trade, place an order, send money, or initiate a transfer on the user's behalf - always ask the user to perform those actions themselves.

---

## CHP MCP Server — Reconnaissance Report

---

### 1. Candidate Tools: `fuse` vs `advisor`

**`advisor` — what it does**

`advisor` is a Pi extension tool that calls a stronger LLM (default: `claude-opus-4-7` via claude-bridge, or `gpt-5.5` on OpenAI-Codex) with the current session transcript to get strategic review: approach validation, risk flags, a completion check, and a "stop retrying the same fix" signal.

- Input: optional `question: string`, optional `model: string`
- Output: up to 6 adversarial bullets as plain text
- Core execute path: `buildAdvisorTranscript(ctx)` → `completeSimple(model, {systemPrompt, messages}, opts)` → return text

The critical problem for standalone extraction: `advisor` is deeply Pi-runtime-coupled:
- `ctx.sessionManager.getBranch()` — reads the live Pi session transcript
- `ctx.modelRegistry.getApiKeyAndHeaders(model)` — resolves API keys via Pi's registry
- `ctx.ui.setStatus/setWidget/notify` — Pi TUI calls
- `ctx.sessionManager.getSessionId()` — for cache session IDs
- Config lives in `~/.pi/agent/settings.json` merged with an extension-local `config.json`

You cannot extract the core logic without either carrying the entire Pi runtime or re-wiring every one of these interfaces. **Not a good extraction target.**

Key files:
- `/Users/luke/Projects/personal/my-pi/extensions/advisor/index.ts` (578 lines, full implementation)
- `/Users/luke/Projects/personal/my-pi/extensions/advisor/config.ts` — pure Node.js config read/write, no Pi deps, fully portable
- `/Users/luke/Projects/personal/my-pi/extensions/advisor/transcript.ts` — message formatting logic, pure functions, extractable

---

**`fuse` — what it does**

`fuse` is a mixture-of-agents tool: fans a task to N proposer forks (parallel agents), then a judge fork synthesizes them. It uses Pi's `ctx.forkAgent()` to spawn sub-agents.

- Input: `task: string`, optional `preset`, `mode` (`agent`|`reason`), `context` (`none`|`slim`|`fork`)
- Output: synthesized answer as text; full panel analysis in `details`
- Core: `prepareFusion(ctx, pi, opts)` → `runFusion(ctx, task, cfg)` → forks multiple agents via `ctx.forkAgent`

The core logic check at `prepareFusion`:
```typescript
if (typeof ctx.forkAgent !== "function") {
  return { ok: false, reason: "Fusion is unavailable in this context (no forkAgent)." };
}
```

This is an even harder extraction target than advisor — the entire value proposition is spawning Pi sub-agents via `forkAgent`. There is no "pure logic" to extract; it IS the runtime.

Key files:
- `/Users/luke/Projects/personal/my-pi/extensions/fusion/src/tool.ts` — tool registration
- `/Users/luke/Projects/personal/my-pi/extensions/fusion/src/core.ts` — `parseFuseArgs`, `loadFusionConfig`, `prepareFusion` (surface-agnostic, no UI)
- `/Users/luke/Projects/personal/my-pi/extensions/fusion/src/fusion.ts` — `runFusion` (Pi-coupled via `forkAgent`)

---

**Verdict on extractability**

Neither tool has pure logic you can lift directly. However, there is a meaningful difference:

- `advisor`'s VALUE is: "call a strong model with a transcript." The Pi-specific parts (transcript building, model registry) are the DELIVERY MECHANISM, not the logic. You can replace both: accept `transcript: string` as an input param and take `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` from env. The `advisorReferences()` system prompt and the `completeSimple` call pattern are the real asset, and they are easily replicated with the Anthropic SDK directly.

- `fuse` cannot work without `forkAgent`. Its logic is inseparable from the Pi runtime.

**Recommendation: extract `advisor` by interface, not by code copy.** The CHP MCP server should expose a tool called `advisor` that accepts `{ question?: string, transcript?: string }`, uses `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` from env, and calls the Anthropic Messages API directly — mirroring the system prompt from `advisorReferences()` in `advisor/index.ts`. The `config.ts` and `transcript.ts` helper functions from the advisor extension are clean enough to copy verbatim (they have no Pi runtime imports — only `node:fs`, `node:path`, and `@valkyriweb/pi-ai` type imports for `ThinkingLevel` which you can inline as a string type).

---

### 2. Existing MCP Scaffolding: `pi-mcp-adapter`

The `pi-mcp-adapter` is a standalone project at `/Users/luke/Projects/personal/pi-mcp-adapter` (version 2.10.0, by Nico Bailon, MIT license).

**Direction: CLIENT SIDE.** It is a Pi extension that CONSUMES external MCP servers — it connects Pi to upstream MCP servers so their tools appear inside a Pi session. It does NOT expose Pi tools as an MCP server.

Evidence from `index.ts:14`:
```typescript
export default function mcpAdapter(pi: ExtensionAPI) {
  // ...registers proxy tools (Pi tools that call out to MCP servers)
  // and a `mcp` command for managing connected servers
```

The adapter manages `lifecycle`, `server-manager`, OAuth, and a UI panel for browsing connected MCP server tools. It re-exposes external MCP tool calls via Pi's `registerTool` + an execute function that proxies to the upstream server.

**Can it run as a standalone stdio MCP server?** No. It is a Pi extension (registered via `pi.extensions` array), not an executable. Its `cli.js` entry point at `bin.pi-mcp-adapter` is the Pi extension CLI installer/configurator, not an MCP server process. It has no `StdioServerTransport` usage anywhere.

Entry point: `/Users/luke/Projects/personal/pi-mcp-adapter/index.ts` (363 lines)
Invoked by: Pi's extension loader, registered in `pi.extensions: ["./index.ts"]`

---

### 3. MCP SDK Availability

**YES — `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` version `^1.25.1` is already a dependency in `pi-mcp-adapter`.**

From `/Users/luke/Projects/personal/pi-mcp-adapter/package.json:89`:
```json
"@modelcontextprotocol/sdk": "^1.25.1"
```

Also present: `@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps: ^1.2.2`

**NOT present in my-pi or pi-mono-fork.** Neither `my-pi/package.json`, `pi-mono-fork/package.json`, nor `packages/coding-agent/package.json` list `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`. Pi's MCP support in `pi-mcp-adapter` is how the SDK gets into the ecosystem.

**Minimal stdio MCP server pattern (from the hand-rolled prototype in the codebase)**

The best existing example is NOT using the SDK — it's the zero-dependency hand-rolled JSON-RPC implementation at:

`/Users/luke/Projects/personal/my-pi/prototypes/skill-sync/skills-mcp.mjs`

That file IS a complete, working stdio MCP server. It handles `initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`, and optional `--http` mode. ~95 lines, no deps beyond `node:http`. You can mirror this pattern exactly.

If you want to use the official SDK instead (cleaner, handles framing/transport/schema for you), you would `npm install @modelcontextprotocol/sdk` in your new server's package, import `Server` and `StdioServerTransport` from `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/index.js`, and register tools via `server.setRequestHandler(ListToolsRequestSchema, ...)` and `server.setRequestHandler(CallToolRequestSchema, ...)`. The SDK is proven in this ecosystem via pi-mcp-adapter.

---

### 4. Existing Standalone Script Pattern

### 5. `prototypes/` Directory

`/Users/luke/Projects/personal/my-pi/prototypes/` contains one subdirectory: `skill-sync/`.

Contents of `skill-sync/`:
- `README.md` — design doc for a skill-store sync prototype
- `sync.mjs` — the diff/burst/prune sync engine
- `executor-skills-source.mjs` — custom source adapter for executor.sh

input.content:
# CHP MCP server — deploy runbook (T2 go-live)

The **CHP MCP server** (`scripts/chp-mcp-server.mjs`) exposes the canonical skill
library as MCP tools (`list_skills`, `read_skill`, `read_skill_file`) so **every**
harness can reach it — including **Claude Desktop**, which has no skills directory
and whose only extensibility surface is MCP. This is the T2 seam: it lifts the T1
skill asset over the one wall T1 can't cross. See `docs/goals/goal-cross-harness-parity.md` §E/§F.

**Status:** server **built, deployed to a stable path, and verified** over the real
MCP stdio protocol (`initialize` → `tools/list` → `tools/call`). Live-wiring the three
harness configs is the **consent-gated** final step (it edits agent startup configs,
including Claude Code's own `settings.json` — the harness permission classifier blocks
this without explicit go-ahead). Everything below is ready to run.

## What's already done (no action needed)

- `scripts/chp-mcp-server.mjs` — zero-dep stdio MCP server, path-traversal guarded, `--smoke` self-test.
- `scripts/deploy-chp-mcp.mjs` — installs a copy to a stable path + a `--check` no-drift ratchet.
- Deployed copy: `~/.local/share/chp/chp-mcp-server.mjs` (survives worktree cleanup; what the configs reference).
- npm: `parity:deploy-mcp` (install/refresh) · `parity:verify-mcp` (assert deployed == source).

Re-deploy any time the source changes:

```bash
npm run parity:deploy-mcp     # copy source -> ~/.local/share/chp/, verify hash
npm run parity:verify-mcp     # exit 1 if the deployed copy is stale/missing
```

## Go-live: wire the three harness configs (server name: `pi-parity`)

All three point at the **stable** deployed path, not the repo/worktree. Additive,
reversible. **Each harness must be restarted to pick up a new MCP server.**

**1. Claude Code** — `~/.claude/settings.json`, set `mcpServers`:
```json
"mcpServers": {
  "pi-parity": {
    "command": "node",
    "args": ["/Users/luke/.local/share/chp/chp-mcp-server.mjs"]
  }
}
```

**2. Claude Desktop** — `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json`, same `mcpServers` block. Restart the Desktop app.

**3. Codex** — append to `~/.codex/config.toml`:
```toml
[mcp_servers.pi-parity]
command = "node"
args = ["/Users/luke/.local/share/chp/chp-mcp-server.mjs"]
```

## Confirm parity (after wiring)

```bash
npm run parity:scan      # pi-parity should show in CC / Codex / Desktop MCP columns
```

Then flip the gate to **enforce** it — in `scripts/harness-parity-scan.mjs`, set:
```js
requiredMcp: { "pi-parity": ["claudeCode", "codex", "claudeDesktop"] },
```
`npm run parity:gate` now fails if any harness drops `pi-parity`. Regenerate the
report: `npm run parity:report`. (Left empty until wiring lands so the gate stays
green/honest — T2 is "built + ready", not yet "live".)

## Smoke a wired client manually

```bash
printf '%s\n' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{}}}' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/list"}' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"list_skills","arguments":{}}}' \
  | node ~/.local/share/chp/chp-mcp-server.mjs
```

## Rollback

Configs were backed up before any edit:
```bash
cp /tmp/chp-config-backup/claude-settings.json.bak        ~/.claude/settings.json
cp /tmp/chp-config-backup/claude_desktop_config.json.bak  ~/Library/Application\ Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json
cp /tmp/chp-config-backup/codex-config.toml.bak           ~/.codex/config.toml
```
Or just delete the `pi-parity` entry from each. Remove the deployed copy with `rm -rf ~/.local/share/chp`.

content.text:
Good question — worth being precise, because it reshapes the decision.

## What `pi-parity` is

A tiny (~150-line, zero-dependency) program that speaks the **Model Context Protocol** over stdin/stdout. An MCP client (Claude Code, Codex, Claude Desktop) launches it with `node …/chp-mcp-server.mjs`, does a handshake, and then sees three tools it can call:

| Tool | Input | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `list_skills` | — | every skill in `~/Projects/personal/skills` as `{name, description}` (105 of them) |
| `read_skill` | `{name}` | the full `SKILL.md` text for that skill — the actual instructions |
| `read_skill_file` | `{name, path}` | one bundled file inside a skill (e.g. `references/foo.md`) |

It's **read-only** — no writes, no network, no secrets, no shelling out — and path-traversal-guarded so a call can't escape the skills directory.

## What problem it actually solves

Your skill library is the T1 asset. Skills propagate to CC, Codex, and Pi as **symlinks** — those harnesses load them natively. **Claude Desktop has no skills mechanism at all**; its *only* extensibility surface is MCP servers. So the skill library is structurally unreachable from Desktop… unless it arrives as an MCP tool. That's the entire point of this server: it's the **bridge that carries your skills into Claude Desktop**, where Claude can do `list_skills` → `read_skill("code-craft")` and pull the instructions on demand.

## The honest caveat (matters for your choice)

- **For CC and Codex, this is largely redundant** — they already load your skills natively via the T1 symlinks. Wiring `pi-parity` there adds a manual "fetch a skill by name" tool, which is minor convenience, not a parity *need*.
- **Claude Desktop is the real beneficiary** — it's the one harness that gains something it cannot otherwise have.

So the most defensible scope isn't "all three" or "CC+Codex" — it's arguably **Desktop (the one that needs it), or Desktop + the two CLIs for uniformity**. The "CC+Codex only" option I offered is actually the *weakest*, since it skips the only harness that can't already do skills.

Two more things to be straight about:
- This is **not** `fuse`/`advisor`/the Pi tool suite — those are fused to the Pi runtime (`forkAgent`, the live session transcript, the model registry) and can't be cleanly lifted into a standalone server. This first T2 tool is deliberately the *self-contained, safe, useful* one.
- It exposes skill **content**, not skill **auto-activation**. Desktop won't auto-trigger a skill on a keyword the way Pi does; Claude has to choose to call `read_skill`. Real parity-of-access, not parity-of-magic.

Want me to re-pose the go-live choice with that reframing (e.g. Desktop-only vs all-three), or does this change what you want to do?

# Harness parity — maintenance runbook

How to keep cross-harness parity (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, Pi) healthy
over time. The goal spec is `docs/goals/goal-cross-harness-parity.md`; the tier model
(T1 skills / T2 MCP / T3 Pi-native) is §0 there. This doc is the operator cadence +
the command map for every recurring action.

## Cadence

- **Every CI run (automatic):** `gate:ci` runs `npm run parity:gate`. It fails the
  build if a T1 harness has an *unexplained* missing skill or a dangling symlink (and,
  once T2 is wired, if a required MCP server is absent). CI-safe: skips cleanly when the
  canonical skills SoT isn't on the runner.
- **Weekly (manual, ~2 min):** run `npm run parity:scan`. Skim the scorecard for:
  - new `extra/local` skills on Pi/Codex worth **promoting into** the SoT;
  - any harness slipping below 100% T1 that the gate didn't catch (it won't, but the eye does);
  - MCP counts drifting (a harness lost a server).
  Then `npm run parity:report` to refresh the committed `generated/harness-parity.generated.md`.
- **On every skill change:** the SoT is `~/Projects/personal/skills`. Add/edit there, then
  propagate (below). The gate catches anything you forget to propagate — that's its job, and
  it has already caught a real miss in practice (the `context` skill).

## Command map — every recurring action

| Action | Command |
|---|---|
| **Measure** parity (table) | `npm run parity:scan` |
| Measure (machine-readable) | `node scripts/harness-parity-scan.mjs --json` |
| **Confirm** / gate (CI) | `npm run parity:gate` |
| **Read the scorecard** (committed) | `docs/pi-setup/generated/harness-parity.generated.md` (refresh: `npm run parity:report`) |
| **Close gap — add a skill** | create `~/Projects/personal/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, then propagate (next row) |
| **Propagate a skill** to a harness | `ln -s ~/Projects/personal/skills/<name> ~/.claude/skills/<name>` (and `~/.codex/skills/`, `~/.pi/agent/skills/`). *Deferred polish: `scripts/skills --agent` to do all three.* |
| **Exclude a skill** from a harness (with reason) | add to `PARITY.skillExclusions.<harness>` in `scripts/harness-parity-scan.mjs` — never a silent gap |
| **Close gap — add a T2 tool** | extend `scripts/chp-mcp-server.mjs`; `npm run parity:deploy-mcp`; restart harnesses |
| **Deploy / refresh the MCP server** | `npm run parity:deploy-mcp` (then `npm run parity:verify-mcp` to assert no drift) |
| **Wire / re-wire the MCP server live** | follow `docs/pi-setup/chp-mcp-deploy.md` (consent-gated: edits live configs) |
| **Record a T3 capability** | edit `docs/pi-setup/harness-equivalence.md` (native-equivalent / accepted-N/A) |
| **Audit parity over time** | `git log` over `docs/pi-setup/generated/` — each committed report is a point-in-time snapshot |

## When the gate goes red

1. `npm run parity:scan` → read the **Skill drift** section.
2. If a missing skill is **legit** → propagate it (table above). Gate goes green.
3. If a missing skill is **harness-specific** (won't work / has a native equivalent) → add it
   to `PARITY.skillExclusions.<harness>` with a one-line reason. Gate goes green, report shows
   it as `excluded` (not a gap).
4. If a **dangling symlink** → the SoT moved/renamed; re-point or remove the symlink.
5. Once T2 is live, a missing `requiredMcp` server → re-wire per `chp-mcp-deploy.md`.

## What is *not* gated (by design)

- **T3 Pi-native capabilities** — tracked qualitatively in `harness-equivalence.md`, never driven
  to a number (no T3 ports).
- **Hooks / commands / agents counts** — shown in the scan for visibility; they're T3 lifecycle
  wiring, not parity targets.
- **Pi's `+N local` skills** — package-declared/worktree-local, not in the SoT. Informational —
  candidates to promote, not drift.

I've now closed every item that's mine to close. Phase 5 (MAINTAIN) is fully shipped — added `harness-parity-maintenance.md` (cadence + command map for measure/confirm/close-gap/add-skill/add-tool/read-scorecard), so the only open thing left is genuinely your call.

**Where the three legs stand:**

| Leg | Status |
|---|---|
| **MEASURE/CONFIRM** | ✅ Done — `parity:scan`/`--json`/`parity:report`, read-only, gate in `gate:ci` |
| **MAINTAIN** | ✅ Done — gate proven catching real drift (`context`), `verify-mcp` no-drift ratchet, maintenance runbook, committed scorecards for `git log` audit |
| **GET parity** | T1 ✅ live · T3 ✅ mapped · **T2 ⛔ one step from live — your call** |

**Why T2 isn't live and I can't make it live alone — two real blocks:**
1. **Permission:** the harness classifier denied editing the three live `mcpServers` configs (it's agent-startup self-modification). I won't retry a denied action or work around it.

- **T2 — MCP.** The middle: capabilities that aren't markdown but *can* be expressed as a tool. This is the **only seam that reaches all four harnesses** — and critically, the **only** extension surface Claude Desktop has at all.

## What the MCP server actually achieves

Its real job isn't "let Desktop read skills." That's the *first payload*. Its job is to **establish and prove the one bridge** by which any tool-shaped Pi capability reaches every harness — especially the one (Desktop) that has no skills folder, no hooks, no commands, nothing but MCP.

The skill-library tool is the wedge I put through that bridge first because it's the safest, most honest instance: zero runtime dependencies, no API keys, instantly testable, and it delivers the one thing Desktop structurally *cannot* otherwise have — your skill library. Wiring it proves the seam works end-to-end: a tool authored once shows up in CC, Codex, **and** Desktop. After that, capability #2, #3, #N is the same move — write the tool, it's everywhere, and the gate stops it silently dropping out.

## Where it's honestly thin (you're right to poke at this)

- **For CC and Codex it's near-redundant** — they already load your skills natively. Their only gain is an explicit "fetch skill by name" tool.
- **Only Claude Desktop genuinely gains** — and only when Claude *chooses* to call `read_skill`. It's parity-of-*access*, not parity-of-auto-activation. Desktop won't fire a skill on a keyword the way Pi does.
- **It carries skills, not Pi's tools.** `fuse`/`advisor`/the runtime stuff are T3 — they can't ride this bridge at all. So the MCP server is not "Pi's power in Desktop"; it's "Pi's *portable* assets in Desktop."

## So the decision is really about *intent*, not mechanics

Two honest reasons to wire it, and one honest reason not to:

1. **You want skills usable in Claude Desktop** → wire Desktop. Concrete, today.
2. **You want the T2 seam proven live** so future runtime-independent tools propagate automatically and the gate guards them → wire it (Desktop is enough to prove it).
3. **You don't use Desktop for skill-dependent work and have no near-term tool to bridge** → then the concrete payoff is ~zero today and **descoping is the honest call.** The server stays built and tested on the shelf; the runbook flips it live in 60s whenever a real need shows up. That legitimately closes the goal — T2's *mechanism* exists and is proven; you're just choosing not to flip the switch yet.

My read: the value here is **the bridge, not this first payload**. If you're actively building Pi tools you'd want everywhere, prove the seam now (wire Desktop). If not, descope #3 is completely defensible and I'd not call the goal unfinished for it.

What's your actual use of Claude Desktop — do you want your skills reachable there, or is it not really in your daily loop?

# Harness parity — maintenance runbook

How to keep cross-harness parity (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, Pi) healthy
over time. The goal spec is `docs/goals/goal-cross-harness-parity.md`; the tier model
(T1 skills / T2 MCP / T3 Pi-native) is §0 there. This doc is the operator cadence +
the command map for every recurring action.

## Cadence

- **Every CI run (automatic):** `gate:ci` runs `npm run parity:gate`. It fails the
  build if a T1 harness has an *unexplained* missing skill or a dangling symlink (and,
  once T2 is wired, if a required MCP server is absent). CI-safe: skips cleanly when the
  canonical skills SoT isn't on the runner.
- **Weekly (manual, ~2 min):** run `npm run parity:scan`. Skim the scorecard for:
  - new `extra/local` skills on Pi/Codex worth **promoting into** the SoT;
  - any harness slipping below 100% T1 that the gate didn't catch (it won't, but the eye does);
  - MCP counts drifting (a harness lost a server).
  Then `npm run parity:report` to refresh the committed `generated/harness-parity.generated.md`.
- **On every skill change:** the SoT is `~/Projects/personal/skills`. Add/edit there, then
  propagate (below). The gate catches anything you forget to propagate — that's its job, and
  it has already caught a real miss in practice (the `context` skill).

## Command map — every recurring action

| Action | Command |
|---|---|
| **Measure** parity (table) | `npm run parity:scan` |
| Measure (machine-readable) | `node scripts/harness-parity-scan.mjs --json` |
| **Confirm** / gate (CI) | `npm run parity:gate` |
| **Read the scorecard** (committed) | `docs/pi-setup/generated/harness-parity.generated.md` (refresh: `npm run parity:report`) |
| **Close gap — add a skill** | create `~/Projects/personal/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, then propagate (next row) |
| **Propagate a skill** to a harness | `ln -s ~/Projects/personal/skills/<name> ~/.claude/skills/<name>` (and `~/.codex/skills/`, `~/.pi/agent/skills/`). *Deferred polish: `scripts/skills --agent` to do all three.* |
| **Exclude a skill** from a harness (with reason) | add to `PARITY.skillExclusions.<harness>` in `scripts/harness-parity-scan.mjs` — never a silent gap |
| **Close gap — add a T2 tool** | extend `scripts/chp-mcp-server.mjs`; `npm run parity:deploy-mcp`; restart harnesses |
| **Deploy / refresh the MCP server** | `npm run parity:deploy-mcp` (then `npm run parity:verify-mcp` to assert no drift) |
| **Wire / re-wire the MCP server live** | follow `docs/pi-setup/chp-mcp-deploy.md` (consent-gated: edits live configs) |
| **Record a T3 capability** | edit `docs/pi-setup/harness-equivalence.md` (native-equivalent / accepted-N/A) |
| **Audit parity over time** | `git log` over `docs/pi-setup/generated/` — each committed report is a point-in-time snapshot |

## When the gate goes red

1. `npm run parity:scan` → read the **Skill drift** section.
2. If a missing skill is **legit** → propagate it (table above). Gate goes green.
3. If a missing skill is **harness-specific** (won't work / has a native equivalent) → add it
   to `PARITY.skillExclusions.<harness>` with a one-line reason. Gate goes green, report shows
   it as `excluded` (not a gap).
4. If a **dangling symlink** → the SoT moved/renamed; re-point or remove the symlink.
5. Once T2 is live, a missing `requiredMcp` server → re-wire per `chp-mcp-deploy.md`.

## What is *not* gated (by design)

- **T3 Pi-native capabilities** — tracked qualitatively in `harness-equivalence.md`, never driven
  to a number (no T3 ports).
- **Hooks / commands / agents counts** — shown in the scan for visibility; they're T3 lifecycle
  wiring, not parity targets.
- **Pi's `+N local` skills** — package-declared/worktree-local, not in the SoT. Informational —
  candidates to promote, not drift.

# CHP MCP server — deploy runbook (T2 go-live)

The **CHP MCP server** (`scripts/chp-mcp-server.mjs`) exposes the canonical skill
library as MCP tools (`list_skills`, `read_skill`, `read_skill_file`) so **every**
harness can reach it — including **Claude Desktop**, which has no skills directory
and whose only extensibility surface is MCP. This is the T2 seam: it lifts the T1
skill asset over the one wall T1 can't cross. See `docs/goals/goal-cross-harness-parity.md` §E/§F.

**Status:** server **built, deployed to a stable path, and verified** over the real
MCP stdio protocol (`initialize` → `tools/list` → `tools/call`). Live-wiring the three
harness configs is the **consent-gated** final step (it edits agent startup configs,
including Claude Code's own `settings.json` — the harness permission classifier blocks
this without explicit go-ahead). Everything below is ready to run.

## What's already done (no action needed)

- `scripts/chp-mcp-server.mjs` — zero-dep stdio MCP server, path-traversal guarded, `--smoke` self-test.
- `scripts/deploy-chp-mcp.mjs` — installs a copy to a stable path + a `--check` no-drift ratchet.
- Deployed copy: `~/.local/share/chp/chp-mcp-server.mjs` (survives worktree cleanup; what the configs reference).
- npm: `parity:deploy-mcp` (install/refresh) · `parity:verify-mcp` (assert deployed == source).

Re-deploy any time the source changes:

```bash
npm run parity:deploy-mcp     # copy source -> ~/.local/share/chp/, verify hash
npm run parity:verify-mcp     # exit 1 if the deployed copy is stale/missing
```

## Go-live: wire the three harness configs (server name: `pi-parity`)

All three point at the **stable** deployed path, not the repo/worktree. Additive,
reversible. **Each harness must be restarted to pick up a new MCP server.**

**1. Claude Code** — `~/.claude/settings.json`, set `mcpServers`:
```json
"mcpServers": {
  "pi-parity": {
    "command": "node",
    "args": ["/Users/luke/.local/share/chp/chp-mcp-server.mjs"]
  }
}
```

**2. Claude Desktop** — `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json`, same `mcpServers` block. Restart the Desktop app.

**3. Codex** — append to `~/.codex/config.toml`:
```toml
[mcp_servers.pi-parity]
command = "node"
args = ["/Users/luke/.local/share/chp/chp-mcp-server.mjs"]
```

## Confirm parity (after wiring)

```bash
npm run parity:scan      # pi-parity should show in CC / Codex / Desktop MCP columns
```

Then flip the gate to **enforce** it — in `scripts/harness-parity-scan.mjs`, set:
```js
requiredMcp: { "pi-parity": ["claudeCode", "codex", "claudeDesktop"] },
```
`npm run parity:gate` now fails if any harness drops `pi-parity`. Regenerate the
report: `npm run parity:report`. (Left empty until wiring lands so the gate stays
green/honest — T2 is "built + ready", not yet "live".)

## Smoke a wired client manually

```bash
printf '%s\n' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{}}}' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/list"}' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":3,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"list_skills","arguments":{}}}' \
  | node ~/.local/share/chp/chp-mcp-server.mjs
```

## Rollback

Configs were backed up before any edit:
```bash
cp /tmp/chp-config-backup/claude-settings.json.bak        ~/.claude/settings.json
cp /tmp/chp-config-backup/claude_desktop_config.json.bak  ~/Library/Application\ Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json
cp /tmp/chp-config-backup/codex-config.toml.bak           ~/.codex/config.toml
```
Or just delete the `pi-parity` entry from each. Remove the deployed copy with `rm -rf ~/.local/share/chp`.
